Subject: VPC endpoints / IP allowlist / mTLS — integration follow-up

Hi Sam / Asha —

Great speaking with you earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Goal: Integrate FinPay backend with Redwood Private for real-time scoring and embeddings/reranker traffic while keeping traffic on your private network (no public egress).
- Questions we flagged:
  - Do you require mutual TLS (client certs) to authenticate to Redwood endpoints, or would API-key + IP allowlist be acceptable?
  - Confirm expected traffic pattern: embeddings/reranker calls vs. model generation. Rough qps and token volume would help sizing.
  - Networking constraints: you'll want private connectivity (VPC endpoints / PrivateLink) and control over egress/DNS. Do you have an existing interface endpoint pattern we should match?

Proposed next steps:
1) Tech deep-dive: 30–45m with your infra/security + Jonas to walk through endpoint options (PrivateLink vs. VPN/peering), IP allowlist ranges, and mTLS details — can you do Fri 4/16 10:00am PT?
2) We’ll share an architecture sketch and sample mTLS config/snippets.
3) If you confirm traffic volumes, we’ll propose a Dedicated/Private sizing and expected latency/throughput.

Attaching a short architecture sketch (next email) and will loop Jonas for the deep-dive.

Thanks — excited to move this forward.

— Lauren

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@finpay.com>

Subject: Re: VPC endpoints / IP allowlist / mTLS — integration follow-up

Thanks Lauren — very helpful recap. A couple quick answers and follow-ups: 

- mTLS: Our security team prefers mTLS for any private integration. API keys alone are acceptable only if we can enforce client certs at the perimeter, but the preference is mutual TLS terminating at your edge.
- Egress/DNS: We currently use AWS PrivateLink for partner integrations where possible. We want to avoid NAT traversal and keep all traffic within our VPCs. Private DNS is used to route partner endpoints.
- Volumes: For an initial pilot, expect ~50 qps of embedding calls (short vectors) and ~10–15 qps of generation/reranker traffic. Peak may be higher depending on campaign loads.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) Do you support client cert provisioning/rotation for customers, or do we need to upload and manage our own certs?
2) Can Redwood provide fixed egress IPs / ranges to add to our allowlist if we can't use PrivateLink?
3) For embeddings & reranker calls, is there any recommended pattern to batch or proxy traffic from our side to reduce TLS handshake overhead?

We can do Fri 4/16 10:00am PT for the tech call. Please include your infra/solutions architect.

Cheers,
Sam
Head of Platform, FinPay
sam.patel@finpay.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC endpoints / IP allowlist / mTLS — integration follow-up

Hi Sam / Lauren —

Thanks — happy to jump on the call today. High-level options and recommendations ahead of our deep-dive: 

Option A — AWS PrivateLink (recommended):
- Setup: Customer creates an Interface VPC Endpoint that connects to Redwood’s Private service endpoint. Private DNS ensures traffic to api.redwood.private resolves to the interface endpoint.
- Pros: No public egress, traffic stays in the AWS network, minimal firewall changes on customer side. Supports mTLS at the application layer.
- Cons: Requires customer to create endpoints in each VPC/region.

Option B — Static egress IP allowlist:
- Setup: If PrivateLink isn't feasible, we can provide a set of static egress IP ranges for Redwood egress nodes (or use a small set of NAT IPs) and FinPay can add those to their allowlist.
- Pros: Works with existing architecture; lower initial setup.
- Cons: Public egress involved; you must accept network transit outside AWS private network.

mTLS / certs:
- Redwood Private supports mTLS for authentication. For Private deployments we can integrate with customer-managed PKI or accept uploaded client certs. We also offer an automated cert rotation helper (signed certs with a rotation window) as part of the Private deployment plan.
- For hosted Dedicated customers, we can support mutual TLS with predefined onboarding (we'll need CSR/CA process details).

SDK & TLS optimization:
- Recommend long-lived HTTP/2 connections to reduce TLS handshakes for high qps (our SDK supports connection pooling).
- Batch embeddings where possible (server-side batching supported) to reduce per-request overhead.

Next steps for today’s call (10:00am PT):
- Walk through PrivateLink steps and IAM role needed to accept endpoint service.
- Confirm whether FinPay wants Redwood to host the service endpoint or to do a cross-account endpoint accept flow.
- Share the attached architecture diagram and small mTLS config snippets (attached).

Attachments: redwood-vpc-architecture-diagram.pdf, mtls-config-snippets.txt

I’ll put together a short onboarding checklist after the call (networking steps, firewall/allowlist, certs, SDK config).

— Jonas
